title: A Robot That Follows a Line: A Camera, a Blob, a PID and a Supervisor, and What a Delayed Camera and a Dead One Do to It

questions.question: What is different about the line follower built here?
options: It uses a real camera in place of a rendered picture
It follows the line with no PID controller at all
It is tuned to be faster than the usual kind
It knows when it has lost the line and stops, through the supervisor of phase 19
questions.explanation: The controller is the PID of 14-01 on a blob measured from a picture. What is added is the supervisor, which turns a lost line into a stop.

questions.question: Doubling the gain from 5 to 8 did what to the error?
options: Halved it, from 0.0152 to 0.0076
Left it at 0.0152 exactly
Made the loop unstable, and the supervisor stopped the robot
Raised it, from 0.0152 to 0.0182: past a point more gain does not help
questions.explanation: From 1.5 to 3 and from 3 to 5 the error fell by about a factor of three each time. Past 5 it turned and rose a little.

questions.question: At 0.8 m/s a 400 ms camera delay did what?
options: Nothing: delay only matters above one second
The loop became unstable, the line left the picture, and the supervisor stopped the robot at x 1.69 m
Raised the error by half, to 0.0669, with no stop
Slowed the robot to half speed
questions.explanation: Up to 200 ms the error hardly moved, and at 300 ms it was 1.5 times worse. At 400 ms the robot swung out until the line left the picture.

questions.question: A gap of 0.6 m in the line was crossed with which debounce?
options: 3 frames (60 ms)
50 frames (1000 ms): a shorter debounce stopped the robot at the gap
10 frames (200 ms)
25 frames (500 ms)
questions.explanation: The gap empties the picture for about a second at this speed. Shorter debounces stopped the robot at the gap; the cost of a long one is a second of driving blind.

questions.question: Why did the first version of the code stop at the start line with a delay of three frames or more?
options: The empty pipe at the start was counted as lost line frames, and three of them are a fault
The camera was not yet switched on
The PID's integral was not reset
The fence was loaded after the first frame
questions.explanation: With a delay, the first frames have nothing in the pipe. That is no data yet, and counting it as a lost line stopped the robot before it had moved.

questions.question: What should the portfolio show for a project like this?
options: A video of the robot following the line
The source code and nothing else
The table, the failure and a black box number, each with the command that makes it
The top speed it reached
questions.explanation: A table anyone can reproduce, with the case where it fails and what the black box held, says more about the work than a run that went well.
